name: remap-ranges
title: Mapping values between ranges
summary: Three readings in their own units (temperature −10…40 °C, gain −60…0 dB, speed 0…120 km/h) normalised with clamp((v − lo) / (hi − lo)) and placed on tracks with lerp; the out-of-range speed pins to the end.
prompt: Show temperature, audio gain and speed on horizontal tracks, each mapped from its own range onto the track, with values past the end clamped.
teaches: Normalise a value to 0..1 once, as a named expression: tTemp = clamp(0, 1, (@temp + 10) / 50)
Map the normalised t onto pixels with lerp(start, end, t): cx = lerp(20, 340, @tTemp)
Clamp before mapping so an out-of-range input (speed 140 on a 0..120 scale) pins to the end instead of drawing off the track
pitfalls: clamp takes (min, max, value): the value is LAST, clamp(x, 0, 1) is always 0 (it is min(max(a, c), b), so only the max has to be in the middle)
lerp(a, b, t) does not clamp: lerp(30, 340, 1.17) is 392, past the track, which is why t is clamped first
A gradient set on the paint stays set when you change the colour: the marker after the gradient track would be painted with the gradient. Clear it with {"shader": 0} in the next paint's ops

Tracks drawn to x = 340 only fit the 360 header width: read componentWidth() into a variable (@r) and use it for the right ends, the gradient and the lerp targets; text that only fits when wide can go in a conditionalOperations on that width

snippets.note: lerp(20, @r, @tTemp): 0..1 onto the track, whose right end @r = componentWidth() - 20 follows the live width
{"shader": 0} clears the gradient before the solid marker

check.describe: The temperature marker sits two thirds along the gradient track (23 °C), the gain bar fills 70 % (−18 dB), the speed bar is full with its thumb at the end and a red "over range" note. Resized, the tracks run from 20 px to the live width minus 20 (@r = componentWidth() - 20) and the values, the formula and the markers stay right-aligned at the same fractions, at 234 and at 540 wide; below 320 wide the formula and the over-range note are left out (a conditionalOperations on @r) so they do not run into the title and the Speed label.
